title: the crew runs on the model config.yaml names, and the board shows which vendor, which model and which CLI version each crewman is actually running, as separate fields, read from the run itself
acceptance: Why. The captain noticed on 2026-09-27 that the board cannot tell which vendor or which model a crewman runs on. identity.json holds name, role, project, task, round and attempt, but no vendor or model. The header's engine badge shows config.yaml's default, not what a round actually runs; that day T-126 was re-dispatched by hand with codex, then cursor-agent, then claude, and the board showed none of it. A second finding on 2026-09-28: config.yaml's `model` is never applied. No adapter passes a model flag, so every claude round since T-117 ran on the CLI's default (claude-sonnet-5, per each run's modelUsage) while config.yaml said `opus-5`, and `opus-5` is not even a name claude accepts (`claude -p --model opus-5` answers `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]`; `opus` and `claude-opus-5-5` both resolve to claude-opus-5-5). The captain approved this task on 2026-09-27, and on 2026-09-28 folded the fix into it, choosing `claude-opus-5-5` for both worker and reviewer. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-127.json, is committed on this branch.

Applied, not only recorded. `model` in config.yaml (top level, `worker.model`, `reviewer.model`) is the vendor's own model name. fm-worker.sh and fm-review.sh resolve the role's model and hand it to the adapter (FM_MODEL). Each adapter passes it with its CLI's own flag: claude `--model`, cursor-agent `--model`, codex `-m`, gemini `-m`. A `--model`/`-m` in FM_ADAPTER_ARGS is refused, so config.yaml is the one place a model is chosen. No `--fallback-model` or equivalent: a round never silently runs on another model. config.yaml's values become `claude-opus-5-5` for the top level and the reviewer, per the captain.

A wrong name is refused before the round, loudly. A model the vendor does not recognise refuses the round with a usage error the board shows (en and zh-TW, naming the vendor and the name), not an outage and not a quiet fallback. Where the CLI can list its models (`cursor-agent --list-models`), fm checks the name against that list; for claude, the CLI's own `unrecognized_model` answer is recognised as that refusal. fm-session.sh's config check reports an unrecognised name as well as a missing one.

Requested versus actual. Each run records `model_requested` (from config) beside `model` (what the vendor reports it used, from the transcript, e.g. claude's modelUsage). When they differ, fm emits `model_mismatch` (added to fm-diagram.sh's routine list), and the board marks that crewman's Model field in the warning colour with both names.

Recorded from the run. Each run records `vendor` (the adapter), `model` (the model the vendor CLI reports it is using), and `cli_version` (the CLI's own version string). It records them in identity.json, in the run's status, and in the crew payloads fm-worker.sh and fm-review.sh emit, as separate fields. `model` comes from what the CLI itself says for this run, never from config.yaml. For example, claude's stream/print output carries the model in its init or result message; take each vendor's source from its docs or a recorded transcript, per adapter, documented in `_contract.md`. When a CLI does not say, `model` is `unknown`, never guessed. A later report in the same run, such as a fallback model, updates it. Runs recorded before this change still load, with the three fields shown as unknown.

Shown as separate fields. The crew detail card gains Vendor, Model and CLI rows, next to T-116's project, task and round fields. The roster gains Vendor and Model columns, sortable and groupable like the others. The ship's name tag stays quiet: at most a small vendor mark, with the name, never the model string. The header's engine badge shows the vendors actually running now, such as 'claude ×2 · cursor ×1', and falls back to config.yaml's default only when no crew is aboard. All new labels in en and zh-TW.

Canary and doctor. `bin/fm-canary.sh` prints each vendor's model and CLI version beside its verdict. If T-121 has merged when this branch is rebased, `fm doctor --sandbox` shows them too; otherwise say so in the round report.

Tests fail-first against main: per adapter, from a recorded transcript, the model and version are extracted, and `unknown` when absent; identity.json and crew events carry the fields; the board API returns them per crewman; the card, roster and engine badge render them (Playwright); and an old run without them still renders. Stubs answer as each CLI does. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate; workers do not run the suite themselves. Also: per adapter, the argv carries the configured model with the right flag; FM_ADAPTER_ARGS with a model flag is refused; an unrecognised name is refused before the round (stub answering with claude's real `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]` shape); and a transcript reporting another model emits `model_mismatch`.
